title: Dispatch BBA 1: A Bell Is Heard Beneath the Market Square
summary: Residents report six strokes at dawn, though no bell remains in the district.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A bell sounded beneath Alderwick's Market Square at 5:40 yesterday morning. The six strokes were heard across the lower quarter, though no bell tower has stood in that district since St. Oran's Fever Hospital was demolished in 1875.

The square stands over the site of St. Oran's Fever Hospital, destroyed by fire in 1874 and demolished the following year. No structure from the hospital remains above ground. The city has never recorded a bell in the foundation.

Market porter Joseph Fenner, who heard the sound from the loading arch, described it as "a call meant to gather people, not warn them." He said the tone was lower than the chapel bell on Westmere Road and seemed to come from beneath the cobbles rather than from any direction above.

The bell sounded again at noon, this time nine strokes. A crowd gathered before the last one. Several listeners reported that the final stroke arrived slightly after the others, as though the clapper had been delayed by something inside the metal.
City surveyors found no subsidence beneath the paving and have left the market open. Dr. Saye cautioned against drilling. "We do not know what the sound is traveling through," she told the council.
